technique.name: Front Kick
technique.description: A controlled lead-leg linear kick designed to reach a target through useful knee lift and extension while preserving support-leg balance, structural control, mobility, and rapid recovery.

cycle.description: Continue from the recovered guard into the next repetition.

non_angle_features.label: Return the kicking foot to guard

steps.step_name: Extend and strike with the ball of the foot

non_angle_features.label: Extend without locking the kicking knee
Stay balanced over the supporting foot
Pull the kicking foot back under control
Fold the knee before lowering the leg
Stay balanced on the supporting leg
Place the kicking foot back in guard

measurement_policy.stance: Guard, right-knee chamber, controlled extension, then cyclic recovery to guard
measurement_policy.primary: Kicking hip, kicking knee, and support knee drive step scoring
measurement_policy.supporting: Upper-body guard and ankle alignment guide coaching without rejecting partially visible repetitions
measurement_policy.movement_style: Right-leg front kick from the same balanced guard used for Jab practice
measurement_policy.measurement_reason: Camera-plane flexion keeps the fast kicking-knee measurement stable; torso, support leg, and hip alignment retain world-space depth.
measurement_policy.missing_supporting_data: Reduce confidence; do not reject the repetition

learning_content.purpose: Develop a useful lead-leg linear kick that reaches the target without sacrificing support-leg balance, joint safety, or recovery readiness.
learning_content.movement_definition: A controlled lead-leg linear kick designed to reach a target through useful knee lift and extension while preserving support-leg balance, structural control, mobility, and rapid recovery.

overview.summary: A controlled lead-leg linear kick. The leg lifts through a prepared chamber, extends along an efficient path, then recoils and returns to a stable ready state rather than chasing maximum height.
objectives: Establish a stable and mobile ready state before lifting the leg.
Lift the knee before extending so the path remains controlled.
Maintain support-leg balance and a controllable center of mass.
Extend to useful reach without forceful terminal joint loading.
Coordinate the hip, knee, ankle, torso, and support leg as one movement chain.
Recoil promptly after the useful reach.
Return to a defensively useful state with mobility for the next action.
safety: Train below maximal height until balance and control are consistent.
Do not forcefully lock the kicking knee.
Keep the supporting foot and leg stable during chamber and extension.
Use clear space and controlled speed.
Prioritize safety, balance, control, then performance.

temporal_model.step_name: Extend and strike with the ball of the foot

coaching: Extend to useful reach, then recoil and recover.

guard-stance.goal: Establish a stable and mobile ready state from which the leg can lift without disturbing balance.
key_cues: Keep the non-kicking side defensively useful.
Use only the tension needed for readiness.
guard-stance.why_it_matters: The ready state is a functional launch position, not one universally correct traditional stance.
guard-stance.transition_condition: Begin the chamber when the support leg and torso are stable enough to lift the kicking leg.

chamber-the-right-knee.goal: Lift the knee into a controlled chamber before extending the lower leg.
key_cues: Avoid chasing height beyond your balance capacity.
body_cues: Knee rises as one prepared unit
chamber-the-right-knee.why_it_matters: A useful chamber separates preparation from extension, making the path easier to control and recover.
chamber-the-right-knee.transition_condition: Extend when the knee is prepared and the support leg can maintain control.

extend-and-strike-with-the-ball-of-the-f.goal: Extend toward useful reach through an efficient path without sacrificing joint safety or balance.
key_cues: Reach without forcing the kicking knee straight.
Use the reference striking surface without chasing maximum height.
what_to_feel: Support leg working with the kick
extend-and-strike-with-the-ball-of-the-f.why_it_matters: Maximum possible extension is not the goal; maximum useful extension under safety and balance constraints is.
extend-and-strike-with-the-ball-of-the-f.transition_condition: Start recoil when useful reach is achieved without losing control.

rechamber-the-right-leg.goal: Reverse the kicking leg promptly after useful reach while preserving balance.
key_cues: Maintain readiness for the next action.
body_cues: Prompt return of the lower leg
Body stays centered over the base
what_to_feel: Less effort as the leg returns
rechamber-the-right-leg.why_it_matters: Recoil reduces exposure and makes the next transition available sooner.
rechamber-the-right-leg.transition_condition: Return when the leg is controlled and the base can accept the recovered position.

return-to-guard.goal: Finish in a stable, mobile state that permits another action.
key_cues: Place the kicking foot back under control.
Settle only as much as needed before the next movement.
return-to-guard.why_it_matters: Recovery means returning to a useful functional state, not merely copying identical coordinates.
return-to-guard.transition_condition: Finish when balance, coverage, and mobility are restored for the next repetition.

principles.title: Kinematics
principles.explanation: The knee and foot should follow an efficient path from chamber through useful reach and back to recoil.

principles.title: Biomechanics
principles.explanation: The hip, knee, ankle, torso, and support leg coordinate to produce and control the kick.

principles.title: Balance
principles.explanation: The center of mass must remain supported while one leg moves and the other provides the base.

principles.title: Stability
principles.explanation: Support-leg control resists unwanted loss of balance without preventing useful movement.

principles.title: Mobility
principles.explanation: A useful recovered state leaves options to move, defend, or perform another action.

principles.title: Joint safety
principles.explanation: Useful reach is preferred over maximum height or forceful terminal extension.

principles.title: Energy efficiency
principles.explanation: Avoid unnecessary height, swing, torso displacement, and tension.

principles.title: Kinetic chain
principles.explanation: The support foot, hip, knee, ankle, and torso contribute as a coordinated sequence.

principles.title: Recovery
principles.explanation: Recoil and return reduce exposure and restore readiness for the next action.

principles.title: Temporal efficiency
principles.explanation: The kick is organized as ready, chamber, extend, recoil, and recover rather than one uncontrolled swing.

common_errors.title: Unstable starting base
common_errors.description: The kick begins before the support side is controlled.
common_errors.why: The lift then creates avoidable balance disturbance.
common_errors.correction: Settle the support foot and torso before chambering.

common_errors.title: Insufficient knee chamber
common_errors.description: The lower leg extends before the knee is prepared.
common_errors.why: The path becomes less efficient and the kick is harder to recover.
common_errors.correction: Lift the knee first, then extend.

common_errors.title: Support-leg instability
common_errors.description: The supporting leg or foot loses control during the chamber.
common_errors.why: The base cannot reliably support the moving leg.
common_errors.correction: Reduce height and speed until the support side stays stable.

common_errors.title: Excessive backward lean
common_errors.description: The torso leans away to create height or reach.
common_errors.why: This shifts the center of mass and slows recovery.
common_errors.correction: Use useful reach under a controlled torso rather than maximum height.

common_errors.title: Forceful knee extension
common_errors.description: The kicking knee is snapped toward a hard terminal lock.
common_errors.why: This increases joint loading and reduces recoverability.
common_errors.correction: Stop at useful reach and keep the extension controlled.

common_errors.title: Slow recoil
common_errors.description: The leg remains extended after useful reach.
common_errors.why: Exposure lasts longer and the next action is delayed.
common_errors.correction: Begin the controlled fold as soon as useful reach is achieved.

common_errors.title: Incomplete recovery
common_errors.description: The foot returns outside a stable, mobile base.
common_errors.why: The technique ends with residual instability and fewer movement options.
common_errors.correction: Place the foot under control, restore balance, then continue.

knowledge_check.question: What should happen before the lower leg extends?

options.label: The knee lifts into a controlled chamber

knowledge_check.feedback: Correct: prepare the knee before extending.

knowledge_check.question: What is the support leg responsible for?
knowledge_check.feedback: Correct: the support leg provides the balance base.

knowledge_check.question: What is the target at extension?
knowledge_check.feedback: Correct: useful reach is more important than maximum height.

knowledge_check.question: What should happen after reach?

options.label: Recoil and return to a useful ready state

knowledge_check.feedback: Correct: recoil and recovery reduce exposure and restore readiness.

rounds: Chamber: lift the knee under control.
Extend: reach usefully without forcing the joint.
Recover: return to a stable, mobile state.
shadow_rehearsal.instruction: Complete 3 slow rounds. Increase speed only if the support leg, knee path, and recovery remain consistent.
